entries.subject: DART final Didymos v003 OBJ series
entries.finding: [DART final Didymos v003 OBJ series](https://pdssbn.astro.umd.edu/holdings/pds4-dart_shapemodel-v1.0/data_derived_didymos_model_v003/) — Included. Direct original mesh, source labels and SIS; the 9.309 m release is adequate for the selected display budget. Higher nominal-resolution versions share the source accuracy/coverage limitations.

entries.subject: Didymos relative-albedo facet table
entries.finding: The retained native FITS-table label explicitly names didymos_g_9309mm_spc_obj_0000n00000_v003.obj and describes relative albedo at facet centers, with facet number, latitude, longitude and radius columns. This supports pairing it with that exact selected mesh. The existing centroid comparison qualifies correspondence; this ledger review read the source label and retained result, and did not rerun the fit. Relative albedo is not absolute I/F or mineral abundance.

entries.subject: Derived topography, slope, gravity and tilt products
entries.finding: The source release includes topography, slope, gravity and tilt fields. The earlier survey cited facet-table decoding as a prerequisite; the current relative-albedo view already uses facet correspondence. These additional quantities remain unqualified and depend on their own density, rotation and reference-surface assumptions. The current Elevation view uses a reference sphere.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-bound scalar recipe verifies this field’s units, assumptions, facet correspondence and invalid coverage on the selected mesh.

entries.subject: DRACO calibrated image mosaic
entries.finding: Two DRACO geometry cubes supply the registered partial-coverage mosaic. The native radius plane separates the bodies before camera fitting; the later partial image takes precedence where it qualifies. This does not qualify LUKE camera registration.

entries.subject: NAIF DART global DSK
entries.finding: [NAIF DART global DSK](https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/pds/pds4/dart/dart_spice/spice_kernels/dsk/) — Excluded duplicate geometry transport. The directly released OBJ already supplies the original indexed shape at an appropriate resolution without a DSK conversion dependency.
entries.revisitWhen: A changed source release adds independently useful geometry or metadata beyond the selected model; compare it before changing the displayed source.

entries.subject: Mission PCK15
entries.finding: [Mission PCK15](https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/pds/pds4/dart/dart_spice/spice_kernels/pck/didymos_system_15.tpc) — Pinned comparison reference; not substituted for the shape-specific pole or radius. It also documents the distinction between Dimorphos's pre-impact rotation and the post-impact dynamic frame.
entries.revisitWhen: Published model-specific definitions, an independently constrained pole/scale, or a released replacement mesh that resolves the recorded ambiguity.

entries.subject: LICIACube LUKE photographs
entries.finding: Measured. The LUKE calibrated collection holds 270 products; all 228 encounter frames fall between 29 and 321 seconds after impact, so every one looks through the ejecta. Short exposures do resolve Didymos: at closest approach, 60.4 km, its disc spans about 166 pixels at the instrument kernel's 78.0 microradians per pixel, and measured disc widths match the kernel prediction to within two pixels at two epochs. A LICIACube kernel bank was built from the thirteen reconstructed kernels the products' own PDS4 labels name, and it reproduces the archive's stated ranges to under a kilometre. Two things stop a lens. The kernels place the body about 0.5 degrees, roughly 110 pixels, from where it appears in the frames, which at this range is about one body radius, so the transfer samples beside the disc as much as on it; the archive's own stated boresight differs from the same kernels by 0.16 to 0.88 degrees per frame, and the header's spacecraft quaternion agrees with it no better. Limb refinement cannot absorb that offset: it leaves 0 of 23 holdout points within 6 pixels, because the body's limb against the ejecta does not match the projected mesh. A prepared lens reached 20% coverage and no verdict, with the outline, cross-frame and relief sweeps all undecided on a round body.
entries.revisitWhen: An attitude solution that places Didymos where the frames show it, within the pixel budget a limb fit can absorb, or LUKE frames of a body whose limb separates from the ejecta well enough to refine against.
